Kit

kit/fx — bursts, flashes, tracers

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Effect lifetimes and tracer timingAPI by taskLocal projectile feedback before authority resultsPool lifetime and callback rulesFloating text (Floats / float_text / floats_frame)Screen shake (Shake / shake_add / shake_frame)

kit/fx creates one-shot particle bursts, hit-flash tweens, and projectile tracers from code without requiring scene assets. Use it for temporary effects created by scripts. Keep persistent emitters, such as a flaming torch or pyre, in the entity's authored scene.

Bursts, flashes, and tweens can run from presentation code in either replication model: cooperative _edge halves and announcements, or simulation _fx halves and declared events. The tracer pool and fire_announce provide cooperative projectile visuals. In a simulation game, projectiles are predicted entities with their own visuals (see sim.md).

This package supports 2D effects only. Bursts use Cpu_Particles2d, floating text uses Control-positioned Labels, and shake moves a Node2d. A 3D game must supply its own effects, including screen shake. These APIs take (x, y); dimension-independent packages such as combat/interact/ai use [3]f32 positions.

Odin
import kfx "godot:kit/fx"

Effect lifetimes and tracer timing#

Flashes and bursts have different lifetimes:

  • flash colors a node immediately, then uses a Tween to return it to white. The node owns the tween, which is released if the node is removed mid-flash.
  • burst_at parents a one-shot spark emitter to the world so it can outlive the entity that triggered it. The game owns a Bursts pool that tracks emitters for BURST_TTL :: f32(0.8) seconds. Call bursts_frame() once per frame to remove expired emitters.

Tracers display a kcombat.Fire, which describes the authority's projectile with velocity in px/tick and lifetime in ticks. Each tracer is a local glyph Label animated per frame in px/s; it is neither an entity nor a network message. The pool advances and tracks nodes and detects contacts. The game handles visual hits through callbacks.

API by task#

Bursts and flashes:

Odin
burst_at :: proc(fx: ^Bursts, parent: gd.Node, x, y: f32, color: gd.Color)
bursts_frame :: proc(fx: ^Bursts, delta: f64)   // remove expired emitters, once per frame
bursts_destroy :: proc(fx: ^Bursts)             // frees the tracking list; nodes belong to the scene
flash :: proc(node: gd.Node, color: gd.Color)   // nil-safe — a victim's node may already be gone
burst_node :: proc(parent: gd.Node, x, y: f32, color: gd.Color) -> gd.Cpu_Particles2d

burst_node returns the configured emitter without adding it to the cleanup pool, for effects whose lifetime the game manages separately. Use burst_at for temporary world-positioned bursts that the pool should remove.

Tracers: the game supplies target and hit callbacks:

Odin
// Return eligible targets for this shooter's tracer; allocate the slice from temp_allocator.
Targets_Proc :: proc(user: rawptr, shooter: knet.Player_Id) -> []kcombat.Target

Tracer_Hit :: struct {
	shooter: knet.Player_Id,
	target:  u32,     // the kcombat.Target id the game supplied (a Net_Id, usually)
	pos:     [3]f32,  // the victim's position (where the sparks go)
}
On_Hit_Proc :: proc(user: rawptr, hit: Tracer_Hit)

tracer_add :: proc(t: ^Tracers, parent: gd.Node, f: kcombat.Fire, glyph: string, tick_hz: int)
tracers_frame :: proc(t: ^Tracers, delta: f64, user: rawptr, targets: Targets_Proc, on_hit: On_Hit_Proc)
tracers_clear :: proc(t: ^Tracers)              // remove active tracers on a level change
tracers_destroy :: proc(t: ^Tracers)

tracer_add converts the Fire's units for frame-based animation: vel = f.vel * hz and left = f32(f.ttl) / hz. Pass ksess.session_tick_hz(&ses) so the display matches the configured simulation rate. Each frame, tracers_frame advances tracers and sweeps each movement segment for contact. It calls on_hit for visual contact and removes that tracer. Expired tracers are removed without a hit callback. The abbreviated signature above omits the optional on_expire: On_Expire_Proc = nil argument; supply it to receive the final position when a tracer expires.

Local projectile feedback before authority results#

Cavecrawl and the latency-injected integration tests demonstrate local projectile presentation before authority results arrive:

  1. The shooter draws a predicted tracer in the frame the shot is cast.
  2. The host launches the authoritative simulation projectile and announces Fire through SES_APP so other peers can draw it.
  3. Receivers skip announcements for their own shots (fire.shooter == me in the handler) to avoid duplicate tracers.
  4. tracers_frame advances each tracer per frame. On visual contact, the game displays predicted hp loss, sparks, and a flash. Later authority deltas supply the accepted hp value.

From cavecrawl's rocks.odin:

Odin
// Display a local rock as a ● tracer in the kit/fx pool; it has no entity or network message.
add_visual_rock :: proc(self: ^CaveLobby, f: kcombat.Fire) {
    kfx.tracer_add(&self.tracers, self.world, f, "\xE2\x97\x8F", ksess.session_tick_hz(&self.ses))
}

// Every peer, once per frame:
cave_visual_frame :: proc(self: ^CaveLobby, delta: f64) {
    kfx.tracers_frame(&self.tracers, delta, self, rock_targets, rock_impact)
}

// Eligible targets are living bodies except the shooter's own avatar.
rock_targets :: proc(user: rawptr, shooter: knet.Player_Id) -> []kcombat.Target {
    self := cast(^CaveLobby)user
    targets := make([dynamic]kcombat.Target, context.temp_allocator)
    for id, sp in self.spelunkers {
        if id == self.avatar_of[shooter] || sp.hp <= 0 {continue}
        append(&targets, kcombat.Target{id = u32(id), pos = {sp.x, sp.y, 0}, radius = BODY_RADIUS})
    }
    // ... dwellers too ...
    return targets[:]
}

An impact can display hp loss through the kcombat.Predicted_Hp overlay, sparks at the victim, and a red flash in the frame of visual contact, without waiting for a round trip. If the authority reports a miss, the displayed hp returns to the accepted value.

Odin
rock_impact :: proc(user: rawptr, hit: kfx.Tracer_Hit) {
    self := cast(^CaveLobby)user
    // ... kcombat.php_note_hit on the victim ...
    fx_burst_at(self, hit.pos.x, hit.pos.y, {1, 0.9, 0.4, 1})
    fx_flash(self.nodes[knet.Net_Id(hit.target)], {1, 0.35, 0.35, 1})
    refresh_hud(self)
}

Pool lifetime and callback rules#

  • Use the configured tick rate. Fire uses px/tick, while tracers use px/s. tracer_add converts between them using session_tick_hz. Hardcoding 20 gives the wrong velocity and lifetime when the session uses another rate.
  • Targets are rebuilt per tracer per frame, from context.temp_allocator. Eligibility depends on the shooter (never hit your own avatar), so there is no cached list. Your Targets_Proc must be cheap and must not return long-lived memory.
  • The library does not log effects. Games supply their own log lines. Cavecrawl wraps calls in fx_burst_at and fx_flash in its fx.odin to emit CAVE_FX lines for integration tests. Use wrappers if your tests inspect effect logs.
  • Advance pools every frame. Call kfx.bursts_frame(&fx, delta) and kfx.tracers_frame(...) to animate and remove expired effects. Run visuals before host ticks in the frame loop so a predicted impact is recorded before authority damage can arrive in the same frame.
  • Choose clear or destroy by lifetime. tracers_clear frees in-flight nodes and retains the pool. tracers_destroy / bursts_destroy release tracking memory; the scene owns the nodes.
  • A visual hit can differ from the authority's result. Play effects from on_hit; never mutate replicated state there. Use the prediction overlay in combat.md instead.

Siblings: combat.md (Fire, Target, projectile_hit, predicted hp) · session.md (session_tick_hz, SES_APP fire announcements) · ui.md (the HUD the impact repaints).

Floating text (Floats / float_text / floats_frame)#

Floating text displays a label such as "+2 wood" or "-14", moves it upward, and fades it out. The game owns a Floats pool and calls floats_frame(&fx, delta) once per frame to animate and remove labels. Parent labels to the world so they can outlive the triggering entity. The engine copies the text, so temporary strings from fmt.ctprintf are valid inputs.

Odin
kfx.float_text(&self.floats, self.boot.world, x - 16, y - 34, "+1 wood")

Screen shake (Shake / shake_add / shake_frame)#

Shake tracks an impact intensity called trauma. shake_add(&s, 0.3) increases it; it decays linearly, and positional jitter scales with trauma². Larger impacts therefore produce disproportionately larger offsets. Apply the offset each frame to Boot's Node2D containers so their contents move together:

Odin
kfx.shake_frame(&self.shake, delta, self.boot.stage, self.boot.world)

For local action feedback, add shake on the acting player's screen using the mine path of a presentation proc, as homestead does. Observing another player's action need not shake the local screen. The final frame restores the containers' original positions.
